SMTO-EXE-0116 — More than one item on the page matches what SMTO was asked to use

GUID: 3cbbefef-6bad-5149-b8a1-46cca062a2b6
Slug: browser-element-ambiguous
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: browser

What happened

  • SMTO found several buttons, fields or downloads that fit the description, so it stopped instead of guessing. Nothing was clicked, typed or saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Tell SMTO exactly which one you mean, for example "the Save button in the pop-up" or "the Email field under Billing address". Pages often repeat the same label, and extra detail lets SMTO tell them apart.
  2. Ask SMTO to look at the page again and list the matching items, then tell it which one to use. Choosing from SMTO's list removes any doubt about which item is meant.
  3. For downloads, ask SMTO to list its downloads and pick the file by its name. Several files arrived, and SMTO won't guess which one you want.

What success looks like

  • SMTO names the single item it will use, and the action or download goes ahead.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with a screenshot or description of the page, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't tell SMTO to just pick the first match; it could click the wrong button or save the wrong file.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The browser locator matched more than one visible element, or a download wait found several new downloads without an exact download_id.

What this means

  • Element matching returned multiple candidates, or download export had several candidates without an explicit ID. The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.

Why this can happen

  • Element matching returned multiple candidates, or download export had several candidates without an explicit ID.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the matching elements/downloads and narrow the semantic locator or choose an exact returned identity.

How to fix it

  • PlaywrightBackend._target and wait_for raise element_ambiguous when the semantic locator returns more than one visible match; _downloads raises it when wait_for_download sees several candidates and no download_id. Use a more specific locator (role plus exact name, label or test_id) or an exact element_ref from browser.snapshot/find; for downloads pass download_id or after_download_id from browser.downloads.
  • Use a more specific semantic locator or select an exact returned element/download reference.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use a more specific semantic locator or select an exact returned element/download reference.

How to verify the fix

  • Exactly one intended target is selected before an action or export.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, scan CDP endpoints, or export cookies/passwords/storage.

Technical notes

  • The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
